narrative.overview:
QuantumLab is a measuring instrument, not a showcase. A navy room (Deep Space) or a clean daylight bench (Light Clean) holds one lit object: the computed orbital, density or molecule on the canvas, or, on the owner's Operate pages, the month's money and jobs. The chrome is quiet, tonal and dense: surfaces step a few points of lightness apart, borders are hairlines, and the only loud colours on screen are the science colours, which mean something, and the status colours, which also mean something. Accent blue marks what you can act on, what is selected, and the single line of money that matters.

Density is deliberate. The viewer is a fixed full-window workstation (top bar; Explore, canvas, inspector) at 13 px body text; the Operate surfaces are scrolling documents on the same tokens, built from one budget strip, a compact chart band drawn on the page itself, and one-line rows that open in place. Every figure carries its unit and its word ("of", "held", "charged", "so far"), set in tabular figures so columns of money and minutes align.

Both themes are first-class and share every structural token; only colour, shadow and the canvas backdrop change. The system is MUI 7 driven entirely from `src/design/tokens.ts` (tokens.css is generated from it), so a new surface inherits the world by importing tokens.css and design.css and using the MUI theme from `theme.ts`.
keyCharacteristics: Tonal navy layering in Deep Space; hairline borders and a light lift in Light Clean.
Science colours untouched in both themes; status colours carry meaning only.
Inter Variable throughout, a narrow ramp (11 to 20 px), tabular figures for every number.
Fixed workstation for the viewer; scrolling ledger for Operate pages.
Short ease-out motion (120 / 180 ms), zero under reduced motion.
Four learning levels decide which controls exist and how deep Info goes; hidden controls leave one quiet line, never a greyed control.

rules.name: The Science Is Not Style Rule
rules.body: Phase, density and ESP colours are never whitened, tinted, darkened or swapped per theme for a look. Where a phase hue falls under 3:1 on its panel (Light Clean's orange), a `swatch-ring` outline carries the contrast; the hue stays.

rules.name: The Meaning-Only Status Rule
rules.body: Green, amber, red and the running-blue appear only where they state an outcome, and every use is keyed (a legend, a chip label, or words). Amber means "past a prediction" at any overrun, with no tolerance, or "billed past the approved maximum, absorbed by the app".

rules.name: The One Blue Voice Rule
rules.body: Signal Blue marks actions, selection and the one money line; it is never a section tint, a decorative stroke or a background wash.

rules.name: The Wordmark Keeps The Violet Rule
rules.body: The violet gradient lives only in the "Lab" half of the wordmark (solid fallback included); it is not a UI colour.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Every number that can sit above or beside another (money, durations, memory, ticks) is set with `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` (`.ql-tabular`).

rules.name: The Phone Fourteen Rule
rules.body: Body steps to 14 px under the phone query; captions and ticks do not grow.

rules.name: The No Shouting Rule
rules.body: No uppercase labels, no tracked-out small caps, no size over 20 px in product chrome.

rules.name: The Typeset Science Rule
rules.body: Names of what is drawn carry real subscripts: an orbital's 3d<sub>z²</sub>, an MO's 1σ<sub>g</sub>, an irrep's 1b<sub>1</sub>, a point group's C<sub>2v</sub> or T<sub>d</sub> (everything past the first letter in a real `<sub>`, so any suffix works), a quantity's R<sub>e</sub>; an underscore is never shown. Signs are a true minus (U+2212); values outside the plain range read "2.66 × 10⁻²", never e-notation. A surface that cannot hold markup (the document title, an export caption, an accessible name built as a string) takes the flat Unicode form ("3dz²", "1b₁", "C₂ᵥ"); a spoken name takes plain digits ("H2O", "1b1", "3dz²"), because screen readers voice Unicode subscript digits inconsistently. One parser feeds all three forms (`src/format/sci.ts`, `src/format/subscripts.ts`, `OrbitalLabel`, `PointGroupLabel`), so they never disagree.

rules.name: The eV First Rule
rules.body: An energy reads in electron-volts first with hartree in parentheses, held on one line: "−5.41 eV (−0.199 Ha)". A difference carries its sign either way ("+9.05 eV (+0.333 Ha)") at three significant figures, so nothing rounds to "−0.00 eV"; a total energy keeps Ha to five places. One Ha→eV factor (CODATA 2018) lives in `src/format/energy.ts`.

rules.name: The Glow Belongs To Deep Space Rule
rules.body: Halos and added light exist only in the dark theme; Light Clean expresses the same states with ink rings and darker rims.

rules.name: The Tonal Scroll Cue Rule
rules.body: A scroller with more below it says so with a tonal fade, not a shadow, glow, arrow or "More": the last ~24 px fade out through a `mask-image` while (and only while) `scrollTop + clientHeight < scrollHeight`. Where the scroller has a hairline under it (Info in the inspector), the mask keeps that last pixel opaque so the hairline stays drawn; the phone sheet, which has none, fades to its edge. The mask is never animated, so reduced motion has nothing to stop. It works the same in both themes.

rules.name: The Glow Finish Is The Owner's Rule
rules.body: The 3D Glow finish (`src/orbital_glow.ts`, GLOW_TUNING) is presentation only and its values were tuned live by the owner; they are recorded there, not here, and are not restyled.

rules.name: The Hide, Don't Grey Rule
rules.body: A control above the reader's level is absent, not disabled. Its place holds one quiet line saying where it appears, or what it still holds; a greyed control is never shown.

rules.name: The Plain First Rule
rules.body: Every explanation starts plain and grows by band. A scientific term with an (i) or a reference never appears below the level its band opens at.

rules.name: The One Home Per Number Rule
rules.body: Each figure has one place on screen. A key number lives in Info's facts, a control's value in that control's readout, a scale in the canvas key; the canvas subtitle is one plain line that restates neither the title nor Info's numbers, and adds the method only at Research. A panel line that would repeat an Info fact is dropped.

rules.name: The One Pressed (i) Rule
rules.body: At most one (i) is pressed at a time, and only the one whose press set the topic; a second (i) for the same term elsewhere stays at rest.

dos: Do take every colour, size, radius and duration from `tokens.ts` through `tokens.css` or the MUI theme; add a role there before using a new value.
Do set every comparable number in tabular figures and pair it with its unit and its word ("$0.04 of $0.51", "1.20 so far of 2.10 GB").
Do draw an overrun in amber however small, and key every status tone in a legend or in words.
Do say an off-scale reference (a cap, a limit) in words rather than drawing it at a false height.
Do open a record's detail in place under its row, one step away, rather than navigating off the list.
Do keep a visible 2 px focus ring on every interactive element and honour reduced motion (hover 120 ms, panels 180 ms, ease-out, 0 ms when reduced).
Do give secondary text a real colour token (`text-2`, `text-3`), never opacity, so contrast tests see the painted colour.
Do hide a control above the reader's level and leave its one-line pointer, or its held-value note while it still holds a value.
Do order Info as title, plain lead, facts, notes, technical, then "How this was computed", and keep Basics and Explore leads to 3 lines or fewer.
Do give each number one home, and set energies eV first with Ha in parentheses.
Do put an (i) beside the word it explains, with `aria-pressed` and `aria-controls`, and let only one be pressed.
Do set names of what is drawn with real subscripts and a true minus; flat Unicode where markup cannot go, plain digits where it is spoken.
donts: Don't whiten, tint, darken or swap the phase, density or ESP colours for either theme or any finish.
Don't use green, amber, red or the running-blue as decoration, section colour or emphasis.
Don't build KPI-tile grids or wide spreadsheets that push cost off screen on Operate pages; use the strip, the band and one-line rows.
Don't set anything under 11 px, or uppercase labels and buttons.
Don't add drop shadows to Deep Space panels or glows to Light Clean.
Don't let the wordmark's violet gradient leave the wordmark.
Don't grey out a control the level hides, or let lowering the level change what is drawn.
Don't print e-notation, a hyphen for a minus, or an underscore in a name.
Don't repeat a figure across the subtitle, a panel line, the canvas key and Info.
Don't cue more content with a drop shadow, a glow, an arrow or a "More" label; use the tonal fade.
